**Title (English, from literature):** Receiving food in a dangerous place

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Catutthapāṭidesanīya* (Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pāṭidesanīya 4) is the fourth and final rule in the *pāṭidesanīya* (offenses requiring confession) section of the Theravāda *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga*. As classified within the broader Pātimokkha structure, the *pāṭidesaniya* category comprises four rules for fully ordained monks, the infringement of which requires formal acknowledgement and confession [von Hinüber 1996]. The regulation concerns forest dwellings: a monk who accepts food in a hazardous wilderness lodging without prior notice must acknowledge the offense. Modern translations of the text include an English rendering by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

Apart from Oskar von Hinüber's structural overview listing the four *pāṭidesaniya* rules in the Vinaya [von Hinüber 1996], the secondary literature search yielded no direct discussions, returning only homonymous citations of other non-Vinaya texts.
